name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: Open-AI released Whisper, an open source speech recognition model with human level robustness and accuracy on English language

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . Trained on 680,000 hours of multilingual and multitask supervised data collected from the web.

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a term that we read often in the media

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . It seems like everyday, there’s a new breakthrough coming up on my social media feed

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . For Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), a subfield of NLP, one of the last advances is a new model proposed by OpenAI: Whisper , a multilingual and multitask neural model with billions of parameters

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . This model can transcribe and translate English audio into 96 languages, along with other tasks such as text normalization, language identification, and voice activity detection

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . The architecture of this neural model is an encoder-decoder Transformer-based neural network that, differently from the unsupervised models based on wav2vec , is trained with 680,000 (weakly) supervised hours of audio collected from the web

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . While wav2vec has provided exceptional results, even more if we talk about low-resource languages, the authors of Whisper argue that this unsupervised model requires non-straightforward fine-tuning to be helpful for a particular task, for example speech recognition on a low-resource language

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . The authors of Whisper then coped with the problem of ASR by following a supervised approach but with some required remarks

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . As previous works have shown: a) using several datasets/domains helped the performance of the ASR system, and b) weakly and maybe noisy but abundant data can also improve de quality of the output of the ASR system

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . These findings paved the way to use this vast amount of web-crawled data from several domains, along with the non-verbatim transcriptions that came with it

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . But they didn't stop there, as they included multilingual data in almost 100 other languages to allow the model to learn the transcription and translation tasks jointly.

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: Regarding data filtering, some interesting points to highlight are: Weakly standardization of text, using transcriptions almost as-is. Removal of automatic transcriptions from other ASR systems to avoid biasing the system to this automatic output. Language identification to clean (audio, transcription) pairs that do not match. Audio files split in chunks of 30 seconds, including voice-empty segments that they use for the Voice Activity Detection (VAD) task.

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: When it comes to the architecture, they do not use an overly complex setup, but a set of Transformer encoder blocks providing the cross-attention scores to the decoder, also based on Transformer

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . This way, they focused on the supervised training method isolating any modeling effect

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . One of the most exciting parts of this work is the multitask orientation of the model, coping not only with ASR but with several related tasks, such as speaker diarization or VAD

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . With this integrated perspective, the authors proposed a token-based interface to identify and select the task during training and inference

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . The following figure illustrates some examples of the sequences they used to feed the model during training, along with the audio-conditioned input via the encoders blocks

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . Example of a token sequence for an English transcription with timestamps (English speech transcription task)

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . Here, the input tokens are provided with the timestamps and the previous context of this sequence (”as i”)

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . Another example for the VAD task, where the model aims to determine if the segment contains speech or not, with an example of not having speech

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . In this case, the encoder may receive, for example, a music segment

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . Example of a token sequence for a non-speech input (Voice Activity Detection task)

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . This last example illustrates how it is encoded in the translation task, indicating the language identifier and the word sequence without including, in this case, the timestamps

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . Example of a token sequence for a Spanish (ES) to English (EN) translation without timestamps (Speech translation task).

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: The authors discussed the robustness of the model, evaluating their proposal along many different datasets and illustrating the multi-domain capabilities with zero-shot competitive performance

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . The following table compares the Whisper model (Large version - 1550M params) with the wav2vec2.0 (Large 960h), with the same performance on the well-known LibriSpeech test-clean but with a relative improvement of 55% across the other out-domain selected datasets

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . The metric here is the Word Error Rate (WER), an error measure (the lower the better) that reflects the minimum number of edit operations (insertions, deletions and substitutions) to transform from the proposed transcription to the correct text

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . According to these results, the proposed Whisper model provides an excellent out-of-distribution robustness

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . ‍ Regarding the multilingual capacity of the model, while Whisper provided impressive results for the low-data benchmark Multilingual LibriSpeech , the results for other state-of-the-art models on the Eurparl-based dataset VoxPopuli are still far behind.

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: When it comes to translation, Whisper model demonstrates good performance on the CoVoST2 task in low and medium-resource settings, outperforming models trained with this limited in-domain data

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . However, it did not improve the results for the models trained on high-resource languages

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . Regarding language identification, the comparison they performed obtained around 80% accuracy for 82 languages from the Fleurs dataset

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . However, they could not compare with other state-of-the-art methods as Whisper only partially covered the languages included in this dataset

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . They also tested the noise robustness of the model, including white noise and pub noise (ambient noise from crowdy environments), showing its good performance and robustness in this potentially noisy environment.

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: As Whisper is trained on 30-second audio chunks, the authors wanted to evaluate its performance on long audio sequences; this is the expected input for real-world tasks, such as lectures or complete TV shows

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . To do that, they apply a transcribe-and-shift where they transcribe the input and then shift the 30 seconds window according to the predicted timestamps, to transcribe the next chunk adequately synchronized

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model
author: Javier Jorge Cano
content: . They compared their results with both open-source models and commercial ASR APIs

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model

content: . The results demonstrated that this model offers an out-of-the-box competitive performance along several long-audio-based datasets.

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model

content: . They have demonstrated that an integrated model trained this way can achieve almost state-of-the-art performance on speech transcription

name: Whisper 🤫 : A multilingual and multitask robust ASR model

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: X has recently unveiled its open-source recommendation algorithm, aiming to offer users greater transparency into the process through which the platform selects and organizes content for display on their timelines

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . X recently open sourced "the algorithm", leading many to anticipate a comprehensive unveiling of the platform's ranking strategies

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Although it's a great open source contribution, this post explains why the hidden secrets of your feed aren't necessarily revealed.

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: Musk's advocacy for open-sourcing the algorithm might have led some users to expect that it would disclose the weights or reasons behind the promotion of certain

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . However, X's recent open-source release of their recommendation system only focused on the model training pipeline, excluding the specific weights or criteria used to determine which posts are promoted

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . This distinction is crucial, as while the release provides insight into the overall structure and process of the algorithm, it does not offer complete transparency into the precise factors affecting the prominence of individual posts on the platform.

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: X's recommendation system consists of a four-stage process, which closely resembles the one used at Shaped

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . The system operates by collecting the most pertinent Tweets from different sources (candidate sourcing), ranking each post using a machine learning model, applying heuristics and filters, and finally, constructing and serving the For You timeline through the Home Mixer

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Although the released system presents valuable insights for developers on building a recommender system, it does not provide X's internal data, resulting in some disappointment among users who were seeking increased transparency.

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: Candidate sourcing is carried out through In-Network and Out-of-Network sources

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . The In-Network source focuses on the most relevant and recent Tweets from users you follow, while Out-of-Network sources find pertinent Tweets outside your network using Social Graph and Embedding Spaces

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Social Graph analyzes engagements of people you follow or those with similar interests, and Embedding Spaces computes numerical representations of users' interests and Tweets' content to establish content similarity

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . With the release of this component, some of the features used by the system have been disclosed and confirmed rumors regarding Musk receiving special treatment for his tweets after taking over the company.

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: The Ranking stage in Twitter's recommendation system is a crucial step where each Tweet is assigned a score based on its predicted relevance to the user

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . This process is executed using a neural network with approximately 48 million parameters, which is continuously trained on Tweet interactions to optimize for positive engagements such as Likes, Retweets, and Replies

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . The model takes into account thousands of features and generates ten labels for each Tweet, representing the probability of different types of engagement

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . The scores derived from these labels are then utilized to rank the Tweets in order of relevance

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . By effectively ranking Tweets, the system ensures that the content displayed on a user's timeline is tailored to their interests, creating a personalized and engaging experience on the platform.

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: In the Filtering stage of Twitter's recommendation system, various heuristics and filters are applied to the curated content to enhance the user experience by implementing product features that cater to individual preferences

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . These filters help create a balanced and diverse feed, ensuring that users are presented with a personalized and engaging timeline

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Some examples of filters applied at this stage include Visibility Filtering, which removes Tweets from accounts a user has blocked or muted; Author Diversity, which prevents too many consecutive Tweets from the same author; and Content Balance, which ensures a fair distribution of In-Network and Out-of-Network Tweets.

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: The Home Mixer is responsible for blending these Tweets with other non-Tweet content, such as Ads, Follow Recommendations, and Onboarding prompts

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . This combination ensures a diverse and engaging user experience on the platform

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Once the Home Mixer has compiled the right mix of content, it sends the finalized For You timeline to users' devices for display, providing them with a curated and personalized feed that meets their interests and preferences.

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: While X's open-source release offers insight into the underlying mechanics of content curation, it is important to note that they have not disclosed the weights that determine specific content appearances in the pipeline

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Despite this, this recommender system plays a crucial role in creating an engaging and personalized experience for X users, and its open-source release marks a step towards increased transparency

name: X's Open Source Algorithm -  Unveiling the code, but not the secrets
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: Dive into the inner workings of TikTok’s awesome real-time recommendation system and learn what makes it one of the best in the field

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: ! Why is TikTok's feed so addicting

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: ? The secret lies in their recommendation engine, it’s precisely what made TikTok one of the largest social media platforms

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Seemingly the feed can read your mind and keep you in the app for longer

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Recently TikTok decided to let everyone in on a secret and released its model Monolith in a paper titled: "Monolith: Real-Time Recommendation System With Collisionless Embedding Table"

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Online recommendation systems are algorithms that are used to make personalized suggestions to users based on their interests and preferences

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . These systems are commonly used by online retailers and media companies to recommend products or content to their users

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . In this post, we’ll dive into the inner workings of TikTok’s awesome recommendation system and learn what makes it one of the best in the field!

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: Building scalable, real-time recommendation systems is vital for many businesses to build great experiences within their products or websites
chunk_metadata: {"Header 1": "What is the problem with current designs?"}

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . However, current deep-learning frameworks (TensorFlow or PyTorch) don’t work well for real-time production scenarios
chunk_metadata: {"Header 1": "What is the problem with current designs?"}

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . This is because: Updating models based on static parameters and dense computations is unsuitable for good performance in recommendations, which rely on dynamic and sparse features. Common approaches are designed with a batch-training stage and serving stage (during user interaction with the product) wholly separated, preventing the model from interacting with customer feedback in real-time. TikTok’s team explains their solution in 3 steps: They crafted a collisionless embedding table while further optimizing it by adding expirable embeddings and frequency filtering to reduce its memory consumption, making it efficient and suitable for deployment to users; They provided a production-ready online training architecture with high fault-tolerance They experimentally proved that system reliability could be traded-off for real-time learning Sounds intimidating
chunk_metadata: {"Header 1": "What is the problem with current designs?"}

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: ? Not to worry, we will go through every single component and break it down, by the end of this article you will confidently understand why you can lose hours upon hours in the app
chunk_metadata: {"Header 1": "What is the problem with current designs?"}

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Ready? Here we go.
chunk_metadata: {"Header 1": "What is the problem with current designs?"}

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: Researchers at TikTok made the observation that for recommendation systems the data is mostly categorical and sparse

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . This means that if we were to embed the data using an ML approach like word embeddings we would not be able to do so with the number of unique features that data for recommendation provides, in comparison the language models can get away with it due to limited vocabulary size

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Using practical experience from the recommendation systems of YouTube and Instagram the hashing trick was decided to be an optimal approach for a large-scale recommendation system

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Let’s dive into the specifics of the one used in Monolith.

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: A hash map is a data structure that allows very fast mapping via a special hash function of some piece of data to a value

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Hash maps are fast and are used by large platforms to efficiently encode the data, so how does Monolith make it better

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: ? Hash maps suffer from an inherent tradeoff that comes with an original design of this data structure called a collision

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Hash map illustration ‍ A collision occurs when two or more pieces of data are mapped to the same output value by a hash function

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . This can cause problems when using hash functions to index data, as multiple pieces of data will be mapped to the same location

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . TikTok’s team developed a cuckoo hashmap to address this

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . In a cuckoo hash map, just as in a standard hash map each piece of data is assigned a unique key, and the key is hashed to determine its location in the array

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . If the location is already occupied by another piece of data, the existing data is "kicked out" (similar to a real-life cuckoo behavior of cuckoo in relation to eggs in the nest) and has to find a new location in the array, using a second hash function

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . This process continues until all the data has been successfully inserted into the array, or until a maximum number of iterations is reached

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . An example is illustrated above

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Here two hash tables T 0 and T 1 used to store the hashed data

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . A value A is hashed and inserted in T 0 , but as B already occupies this place it is then evicted and an attempt is made to insert it in T 1 , this process will repeat until all values are inserted or the rehashing happens to avoid cyclic insertions

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . This process allows for the avoidance of collisions and it has a significant effect on the performance of the production model

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . To complete their embedding system design researchers added a few bells and whistles to further optimize the process, in particular, to cut the memory requirement that hashing would require: A probabilistic filter to filter IDs in the hashmap.  Since an important observation is that in data from TikTok IDs are long-tail distributed, where popular IDs may occur millions of times while the unpopular ones appear no more than ten times, there is a reasonable assumption to be made that they will not affect the final model quality and therefore can be cleared. An ID existence timer that controls the erasure of old and stale IDs. This could possibly be due to a user that is no longer active, or a short video that is out-of-date. Storing embeddings for these IDs could not help the model in any way so it is sensible to clear the memory.

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: Now as we learned how the data is represented inside the model we need to understand how it is trained and updated

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . The overall diagram of the Monolith online training architecture can be found below: It looks complicated but actually, it all revolves around a very simple process that is the basis for the larger architecture and that drives the core of the overall training architecture

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . TensorFlow's distributed Worker-ParameterServer (or simply PS ) model is a way of training machine learning models in a distributed fashion, where multiple machines (or processes on a single machine) work together to train the model, illustrated below: In this model, there are two types of processes: workers and parameter servers

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . The workers are responsible for performing the computations required to train the model, such as calculating gradients or updating model parameters

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . The parameter servers are responsible for storing the current state of the model, such as the model weights or biases

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . The training is divided between batch training and online training stages: Batch training stage . This stage works as follows: in each training step, a training worker reads one mini-batch of training examples from the storage, requests parameters from PS, computes a forward and a backward pass, and finally pushes updated parameters to the training PS. Batch training is useful for training historical data when there is a need to modify model architecture and retrain the model; Online training stage . After a model is deployed to online serving, the training does not stop but enters the online training stage. Instead of reading mini-batch examples from the storage, a training worker consumes real-time data on-the-fly and updates the training PS. The training PS periodically synchronizes its parameters to the serving PS, which will takeeffect on the user side immediately.

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: To make sure that Monolith can seamlessly switch between batch training and online training it was built with a streaming engine component: In order to gather real-time user feedback for further training the research team used Kafka queues , one queue logs the user actions (click’s, likes etc.) another one is for features coming from a model server

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Then two are joined by using Apache Flink joiner , this data packed is transformed into the training data that is then is read by another Kafka queue, those training examples are used for both batch training and online training: During batch training, data from the Kafka queue is dumped to Hadoop Distributed File Storage (HDFS) ,  after a certain amount of training data is accumulated it is then sent to the training worker For online training the process is simpler: the data is just read directly from the Kafka queue After the training operation is performed a PS collects parameters and according to a selected synchronization schedule updates the serving PS which in turn updates the model on the user side.

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: The joiner process is actually a bit more complicated and we should note a few things about it: In-memory cache and KV(Key-Value)-store , are two components that help stabilize the latency between user actions and features coming from the server, this is due to the fact that they both arrive irrespective of each other’s arrival time, so caching is required to correctly pair them up

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . But what if the user takes a long time to complete an action

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: ? Then caching would not be such a great idea, hence some values are stored on the disk to be paired up again

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . When a user action log arrives, it first looks up the in-memory cache and then looks up the key-value storage in case of a missing cache

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Note also one last step which is Negative Sampling

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . As there are positive and negative examples during training

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . In a recommendation system, positive examples are items that a user likes or has shown interest in, while negative examples are items that the user does not like or has not shown interest in

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . But their amount can be imbalanced therefore it is important to correct this bias in the dataset

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . And that’s it

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: ! You’ve learned about all of the components in Monolith

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Now for one last section where researchers prove the effectiveness of online learning on the fly.

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: Here the team also compared the performance of the model at different sync time intervals to verify the performance: As we can see above online training is essential for better performance of a recommender system with dynamic feedback.

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: ‍ Thanks for reading my deep dive on how TikTok's real-time recommendation system works

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . I hope you found it interesting and learnt something new

name: The Secret Sauce of Tik-Tok’s Recommendations
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . If you have any questions or would like to test a real-time recommendation system, feel free to reach out to the Shaped team at hello@shaped.ai

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: Dive into the inner workings of Google AI’s awesome language modeling approach to audio generation

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: ! Among all the recent hype regarding OpenAI’s ChatGPT, a few prominent industry players in AI are getting ready to release their new fantastic generative models

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . If ChatGPT is well suited for tackling text, the team at Google AI decided to go further and create a model capable of generating sound, in the new paper titled AudioLM: a Language Modeling Approach to Audio Generation, presents a new framework for generating high-quality sound, ranging from different kinds of human speech to musical instruments from sound alone

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Unlike previous approaches, the team found a way to not use text transcription or MIDI representations for the piano

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Generating realistic audio is a complex task that involves modeling information at different scales

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Just as music combines individual notes to create complex melodies, speech uses phonemes and syllables to form words and sentences

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Music is challenging as well, as not only the appropriate notes are required, but to generate new pieces, the model would need to keep the pace and style intact

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Both of these tasks increase in complexity if we want to generate something natural and of high quality

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Sound in fact is sometimes considered a more challenging task compared to text and we will see why soon

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . This, however, didn’t stop the team at Google from achieving a new milestone with their AudioLM model

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . In this post, we will dive into key ideas that power AudioLM, explain why and how they are important, and divine the potential impact of this new innovation for the future of AI.

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: Sound at its core is one of the essential ways for us to experience the world

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . From the myriad of languages, we use to communicate to music to figure out what is wrong with your old car’s engine

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . The physical properties of sound as a wave are a double-edged sword, on one hand, our knowledge of signal processing is what allows us to model it but the complexities of working with signals are also what makes it so challenging

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Audio signals are complex, multi-layered entities that can consist of speech, music, or environmental sounds

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Analyzing audio signals requires an understanding of multiple scales of abstractions

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . For example, speech can be analyzed at a local level, such as acoustic or phonetic analysis, as well as at a higher level, including prosody, syntax, grammar, and semantics

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Similarly, music has a long-term structure but is composed of non-stationary acoustic signals that can be challenging to synthesize

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . In the field of audio synthesis, achieving high audio quality while maintaining high-level consistency remains a significant challenge, especially in the absence of strong supervision

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Recent audio synthesis models have made remarkable progress by using techniques such as autoregressive waveform modeling , adversarial training, and diffusion, resulting in nearly veridical signal quality

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . However, these models often require strong conditioning, such as linguistic features or a MIDI sequence, to generate structured audio

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Without such conditioning, even powerful models like WaveNet can generate incoherent and messy audio.

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: AudioLM solves this by using audio-only information

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . To achieve this they used 2 following innovations: Smart Tokenization Mixed architecture

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: All language models that utilize transformers rely on tokenization, which is a method of encoding text and speech into tokens are usually words or subwords that are separated by spaces or other punctuation marks

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . The purpose of tokenization is to transform the text into a format that can be easily processed by machine learning algorithms

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . It is crucial to have quality tokenization as this allows the model to gain an accurate representation and understanding of complex audio waves

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . To reach the goal of learning from audio alone Google AI team sent the sample audio to two tokenizers

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . SoundStream (also developed by Google AI) performed acoustic tokenization, in Figure 1 to get the tokens, they extracted latent vectors from the compressed embedding space, these tokens carry the information about the acoustic properties of our chosen audio sample, like pitch, intonation, etc

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Figure 1: Overview of the tokenizers used in AudioLM

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . The acoustic tokens are produced by SoundStream and enable high-quality audio synthesis

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . The semantic tokens are derived from representations produced by an intermediate layer of the w2v-BERT model and enable long-term structural coherence

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . But as they discovered, straight acoustic information without any meaning behind it doesn't work well for generating new audio

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Here are a few examples of reconstructed sound using acoustic tokens only: Reconstruction So if the meaning of audio or semantic information is required how do we get it

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: ? To do this we need to utilize a model that can parse audio into words

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . For this task researchers used a pretrained w2v-BERT model, specifically they were interested in the encoding of the audio data that carry semantic information

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . 💡 Key Idea 1: We need only a semantic representation of audio, not the deconstructed text

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . This means what we get from intermediate layers is more of a representation of relationships between different sounds, and their ordering, which sounds naturally sound appropriate together, rather than words

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Figure 2: w2v-BERT architecture

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Two important components are conformer blocks and an MLM block, from which intermediate representation is computed

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . K-Means is then used to cluster the embeddings and centroids are used as tokens

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Your next question, however, might be: okay, speech is fine and well but how do you capture the semantic information of a piano piece

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: ? And the answer is: in the same way

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Since we don't need the actual text, we can use the power of w2v-BERT to add additional structural information about our sound sample.

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: AudioLM’s architecture is the following: A tokenizer model, which maps x into a sequence of discrete tokens from a finite vocabulary A decoder-only Transformer language model that operates on the discrete tokens, performs 3 different types of acoustic modeling (Figure 3) A detokenizer model, which maps the sequence of predicted tokens back to audio The most interesting component is the Transformer model, which contains 3 stages that increase audio quality, researchers found that using a single tokenization scheme doesn't achieve good results, therefore AudioLM does audio modeling using 3 stages illustrated in Figure 3

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . 💡 Key Idea 2: SoundSream has a residual structure, the further the residual quantizer is the finer the acoustic representation

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . This concept is used to get coarse and fine acoustic tokens, the main difference is how far in the layers the representation is extracted (note Figure 3) Figure 3: 3 levels of tokenization

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . 1) Semantic tokens from w2v-BERT; 2) A combination of semantic tokens and coarse acoustic representation extracted early in the layers of SoundStream; 3) Addition of fine acoustic tokens

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: To make sure that the tokenization process produces good quality representations of an audio sample, the researchers used three metrics: ABX, sWUGGY, and sBLIMP

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Left: ABX (↓) scores achieved by the (unquantized) embeddings extracted from different layers of the MLM module of w2v-BERT

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Right: Scores on the development sets of sWUGGY (↑) and sBLIMP (↑) obtained with different numbers of k-means cluster centers for layer 7 ABX evaluation is used to evaluate the performance of different models in tasks such as speech recognition, text-to-speech synthesis, and machine translation. sWUGGY (short for "smoothed Word-Usage Goodness GOF") measures the similarity between the word usage in the generated text and the word usage in a reference corpus. This metric is designed to penalize the use of uncommon or inappropriate words in the generated text. sBLIMP (short for "smoothed Bilingual Evaluation Understudy with Punctuation") is a metric that compares the generated text to a reference text using a machine translation approach. It measures the quality of the generated text in terms of fluency, grammar, and meaning preservation, while also taking into account punctuation and word order. This allowed researchers to select layer 7 as the most promising layer for extracting embeddings and k=1024 clusters for an amount of tokenization

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . And now let’s hear some results!

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: Original Prompt Continuation (AudioLM) Continuation (AudioLM)

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: Original Prompt Continuation (Acoustic-only model) Continuation (AudioLM)

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: AudioLM’s results are undoubtedly impressive, this milestone is a promising step in a direction of future potential research like multilingual speech generation, the generation of music using different instruments all at once, and producing quality informative audio content

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . But the authors of the paper also acknowledge that this result doesn't come without risks

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . AudiLM by the nature of its architecture also inherits all the problems of LLMs, there is no guarantee that the model will replicate dialects and accents well from the groups underrepresented in the training dataset

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . There can be societal biases coming from the generated audio content, and not to forget that short and coherent audio modulation gives rise to a risk of breaching the biometric identification, with that in mind researchers closed a paper with their tool to identify audio that was generated by AudiLM

name: Sounding The Secrets Of AudioLM
author: Heorhii Skovorodnikov
content: . Reference ‍Borsos, Zalán, et al

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: This year’s recommender systems summit included a great set of speakers, each one sharing unique learnings on working with recommender systems

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . ‍ In this post, we summarize the takeaways of each talk and provide some of our thoughts from Shaped.

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: Jacopo Tagliabue, Director of AI at Coveo - Twitter Here Jacopo provided a tutorial on how to build an end-to-end offline recommender system

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Following his tutorial you could build a recommendation system with the following components from data ingestion to serving the predictions: ‍ The content of the tutorial covered key components of a recommender system and was easy-to-follow

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . It gives an example of what the first iteration of a recommender system looks like at many companies (or even their final one)

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . It covered everything from data ingestion to serving the model predictions with a cache

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . As an added bonus, the tutorial used the H&M fashion dataset , which was recently released at Kaggle

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Our infrastructure shares some core designs with the one seen in this tutorial

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . We support data ingestion from different data warehouses and create the necessary pipelines to give life to a recommender system

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . While online serving is often ideal for recommender systems (often the fresher features are the more relevant recommendations are) the extra engineering complexity doesn’t always make it worth it

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Serving recommendations from a cache is the right starting point.

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: Chip Huyen, Co-Founder and CEO, Claypot AI - Twitter In this talk Chip Huyen gave a superb introduction to the online serving side of recommender systems

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . If you read some of her content this presentation would be familiar to you with an added spin for recommendation use-cases

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . It started with the first step on how to move a traditional offline system to online: computing features in time for the model

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Session-based recommenders were also mentioned but not much on the differences in how their backend varies from a traditional ranking system

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Chip then moved to engineering challenges of serving recommendations online: Stateless vs stateful processing of features. Inconsistencies between train and predict data. Monitoring model performance, batch vs real-time. Monitoring data drifts: How does the training data change, what types of data shifts exist, or even when should a newer model be released to production. Monitoring features and model predictions to better help understand model performance and data drifts. The presentation focused on the MLOps and engineering challenges of recommender systems, which are typically the bottleneck to bringing machine learning to production —particularly as models are becoming more general and self-serve

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Perfect balance between complexity and key concepts at recommender systems.

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: Bryan Bischof, Head of Data Science, Weights & Biases - Twitter , Slides Bryan gave a pragmatic talk on working with recommender systems on his learnings working at Stitch Fix, an online fashion company that provides tailored outfits for their customers
chunk_metadata: {"Header 3": "An Embarrassment of Riches; Trying to Find Harmony Among Several Different Models"}

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . He raised many points on working with recommenders and how they affected his work: The difference between recommending physical objects and digital objects. How they had to leverage stock and warehouses. This is something that large e-commerce companies like H&M, Zara and Zalando experience but rarely mention in their recsys content. The existence of different recommender cases (loss functions) in their business and how they leverage them. The dilemma between many specific models vs a big model to cover them all. Political or organizational biases influence their models. While most of the time is business knowledge that gives the edge performance to the recommender systems is easy to overstep and cause more damage. How to best evaluate new roll-outs and AB testing. He went through some of the mistakes they did and how they affected them. He then explained on his current company Weights & Biases could help with the monitoring of some of those points
chunk_metadata: {"Header 3": "An Embarrassment of Riches; Trying to Find Harmony Among Several Different Models"}

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . It was a very approachable talk and in contrast to other speakers that talked about “things to do” Bryan talked about “things not to do”.
chunk_metadata: {"Header 3": "An Embarrassment of Riches; Trying to Find Harmony Among Several Different Models"}

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: Ehsan Saberian, Senior Research Scientist, Netflix - Twitter Netflix gave a very production-focus view on best practices recommender systems
chunk_metadata: {"Header 3": "RecSysOps: Best Practices for Operating a Large-Scale Recommender System"}

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Ehsan went through multiple experiences from his work and summarized a few best practices for the audience: Measure the usage of their service across other systems/teams. Reducing the gap between producer and consumer allowed his team to early detection of multiple bugs. Embrace communication with teams using their recommendations and create as many tools as they need to monitor the performance. If a team has a metric to track related to the recommendation system then add it to your monitoring services. Be reactive to your monitoring services, use it as a way to prioritize work as is a very tangible measurement of your system performance. Log everything! Not necessarily all the data but at least portions of every data source; something like 5% of the served predictions. This helped them debug issues while keeping logs size manageable. The main point from Ehsan was monitoring , tracking what is important for the teams that consume recommendations, and having the necessary data to debug whatever issue appears
chunk_metadata: {"Header 3": "RecSysOps: Best Practices for Operating a Large-Scale Recommender System"}

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . This is something that resonates with us at Shaped as we try to do the same in our systems.
chunk_metadata: {"Header 3": "RecSysOps: Best Practices for Operating a Large-Scale Recommender System"}

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: Even Oldridge, Senior Engineering Manager for Recommender Systems, NVIDIA - Twitter Even gave a summary of their journey building Merlin
chunk_metadata: {"Header 3": "Building an Open-Source Framework for Recommender Systems"}

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . He talked about how they first started with model experimentation, moving now towards model deployments, and how they plan to tackle monitoring and production maintenance
chunk_metadata: {"Header 3": "Building an Open-Source Framework for Recommender Systems"}

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . One of the highlights they mentioned was the recent release of Merlin-system , which goes beyond the models and feature engineering tools they’ve released, and builds out a structure for deploying multi-stage recommendation systems in production.Even mentioned that most companies still take 6-months+ to deploy a recommendation system in production and ultimately their goal is to reduce that time
chunk_metadata: {"Header 3": "Building an Open-Source Framework for Recommender Systems"}

name: Takeaways from the Nvidia Recommender Systems Summit 2022
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . At Shaped, we’ve been following the Merlin library development closely and are excited to start using several of their tools, particularly as we move more towards a GPU-first infrastructure.
chunk_metadata: {"Header 3": "Building an Open-Source Framework for Recommender Systems"}

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: Recently, Meta announced the release of a new AI language generator called LLaMA

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . While tech enthusiasts have been primarily focused on language models developed by Microsoft, Google, and OpenAI, LLaMA is a research tool designed to help researchers advance their work in the subfield of AI

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . In this blog post, we will explain how LLaMA is helping to democratize large language models

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . LLaMA is a large language model introduced by Meta to push the boundaries of what smaller language models can do

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . It is based on traditional transformer architecture and includes some recent training advances such as Pre-normalization (as seen in GPT-3), SwiGLU activation function (used in PaLM), and Rotary Embeddings (applied in GPTNeo)

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . The model comes in four different sizes: 7B, 13B, 33B, and 65B parameters

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . All sizes perform extremely well compared to the current state of the art while having fewer parameters

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . For example, LLaMA-13B performed better than GPT-3 (175B) in most tests or evaluations despite being more than 10× smaller

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . On the other hand, LLaMA-65B, is comparable to some of the best-performing models such as Chinchilla70B and PaLM-540B

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Higher scores are better.

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: Achieving state-of-the-art results with magnitude less of parameter sizes is a huge accomplishment and is beneficial for both research and industry use cases

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . By reducing the computational resources required for training and inference, smaller models are more accessible to researchers and practitioners with limited resources

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . This means that language models can become a part of our daily workflows with ease

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Do you want ChatGPT integrated into your home assistant

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: ? This is what we need to make that happen

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Moreover, smaller models are less prone to overfitting and more capable of generalizing to new data, making them dependable and robust in real-world settings

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . These models are not only energy efficient but also reduce the environmental impact of training and deploying them

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Larger models still outperform smaller ones, as shown by the better results achieved by the bigger LLaMA size (65B) in the first table

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . However, practicality is a key consideration, and smaller models are often more useful for retraining with recent data or fine-tuning for specific tasks

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . These adjustments can yield greater improvements than simply increasing model size, and smaller models are easier to work with than larger ones

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . In fact, it would only cost a tenth of the resources to train a 7B LLaMA compared to a 65B one, as shown in the table

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: The potential for biases in AI language models is a serious concern

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . It's why companies are cautious when adopting them for production systems

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Take Google, for instance

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Despite impressive academic work around large language models, they were slow productionize AI models until OpenAI’s ChatGPT came along

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Google clearly had the AI innovations, infrastructure, talent, and distribution to release Bard AI earlier, but potentially because of the bias issues the risk wasn’t worth it until there was a competitor like ChatGPT

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . The Meta AI team put LLaMA to the test to see if it exhibited any biases towards gender, religion, race, sexual orientation, age, nationality, disability, physical appearance, or socio-economic status

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . They also measured how toxic the model's responses using PerspectiveAPI, an open API to measure toxicity

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . To measure biases, the researchers used stereotypical sentences related to a topic and measured the model's preference using perplexity in a zero-shot setting

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Higher scores indicate greater biases

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . The LLaMA model had the lowest average bias score of 66.6 across all categories, but the score varied in each category

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . The model had the lowest bias score of 57 for race/color, which is excellent

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . However, it had the highest bias score of 81 for sexual orientation, which is not so good

content: The LLaMA model represents a significant breakthrough for natural language processing, with exciting implications for both research and industry

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . By reducing model complexity and footprint, we can make this technology more accessible to a wider range of industries

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Recent research, however, has been focused on increasing model performance at the cost of model size - like the 540B PaLM model

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Thankfully, the 13B LLaMA model has shown that smaller models can outperform their larger counterparts like GPT-3, effectively flipping the script on the size-to-performance ratio

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . Not only that, but LLaMA also has lower biases compared to other language models

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . This breakthrough demonstrates that it's possible to achieve impressive results with smaller models while also reducing the risk of perpetuating harmful biases

name: Size Isn't Everything - How LLaMA  democratizes access to Large-Language-Models
author: Jaime Ferrando Huertas
content: . This paves the way for more accessible and practical applications of natural language processing that are more inclusive and trustworthy
